newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Euroshares pause after record breaking start.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Euroshares pause after record breaking start.

text.p: European shares paused after rewriting the record books on Tuesday morning, encouraged by another closing peak on Wall Street, its 14th this year.
Wall Street was up a further eight points by the European midafternoon, but Europe's three key bourses were well below the new trading highs they rang up in early trade.

The FTSE shot up to a new high of 4,466.3 within minutes of opening, beating the previous all-time high of 4,440.8 set on Monday, but a few doubts about the Dow halted the advance and by 1545 GMT it was only 12.5 points higher at 4,449.9.

Dealers said the FTSE could attack even loftier levels if Wall Street remained strong. U.S. traders said the Dow looked set to break through the 7,100 level but were less confident that it could maintain this advance.
"We got another big boost from the Street this morning
but some people are asking how long that can continue," one London dealer said. "But people have been calling the top for Wall Street for some time and it keeps confounding expectations."
Dealers said there had been good two-way business, with profit-taking hitting some stocks as they reached higher levels but enough investors buying stock to keep the market firm.
"We have seen a bit of profit-taking in places but it's been outweighed by good buying interest," the dealer said. "The prevailing opinion is that the market still has further to go."
The FTSE and the other European markets got an early boost from the Dow, which jumped 78 points on Monday having been up 19 when London closed.

The market was also helped by positive reaction to blue-chip annual results, and a more optimistic view of Britain's interest rate outlook following Monday's comments by Bank of England governor Eddie George.
French shares gave back some of the day's advances, tracking profit-taking on the dollar, traders said.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 18.27 points at 2,690.94 at 1545 GMT.
Germany's DAX index ended a lively floor session at its second record closing high in a row, up 0.72 percent at 3,460.40, though it was off the trading high of 3,474.98 reached earlier.
Demand for blue-chips declined sonwehat after a strong early surge, though the fundamental trend remained intact and the market looked set to challenge the 3,500 level, dealers said.
"There is nothing around to break this momentum," one dealer said earlier. "There is no sign here of a consolidation."
In currencies, the dollar was close to intraday highs at the European midafternoon after bouncing from just below 1.70 German marks in early trading.
Analysts said the fundamental U.S. economic backdrop remained bullish for the dollar and traders said it was supported by strong bids below the psychologically-important 1.70.

U.S. asset market trends also helped underpin the currency, which stood around 1.7060 marks against 1.7027 late on Monday, having touched an overnight low of 1.6975. Chartists saw strong support at 1.6975, from a three-month-old rising trendline.

"The dollar is still hovering around and it's still looking pretty weak, but strong bids pushed it up above those levels (1.70) and that sentiment has gone across the dollar board," said Stewart Newnham, market economist at First Chicago here.
Some dealers said that overnight dollar weakness merely constituted a continued technical correction and a period of consolidation after fresh 34-month highs were scaled last week.

Concerns over the launch date of EMU have also been a cap on dollar/mark recently. But a series of Bundesbank comments late Monday in favour of EMU starting on time acted to undermine mark support in Europe.

"The economic fundamentals and interest rate outlook as well as the strength of the Dow still all point to a higher dollar," Lee Ferridge, currency strategist at Commerzbank in London, said earlier. Moreover, "the Bundesbank are clearly now acting together to calm market fears of an EMU delay."
CURRENCIES AT 1545 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.7060 marks and 121.90 yen compared with 1.7027 marks and 121.74 yen in late European trade on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS 1545 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 12.5 points at 4,449.9.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 18.27 points at 2,690.94.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed up 24.52 points at 3,460.59 points.
PRECIOUS METALS 1545 GMT
Gold fixed at $351.95 an ounce after closing at $350.75 in London on Monday.
